definitions.explanation: The body of law governing private relations between individuals, including property, contracts, family, and inheritance. In Japan, refers specifically to the Civil Code (民法典).

examples.japanese: {民法|みんぽう}が{改正|かいせい}された。
{相続|そうぞく}に{関|かん}する{規定|きてい}は{民法|みんぽう}に{定|さだ}められている。
examples.english: Provisions regarding inheritance are set out in the civil code.

examples.japanese: {婚姻|こんいん}{年齢|ねんれい}の{引|ひ}き{下|さ}げを{含|ふく}む{民法|みんぽう}の{大幅|おおはば}な{改正|かいせい}が{国会|こっかい}で{審議|しんぎ}されている。
examples.english: A major revision of the civil code, including lowering the marriage age, is being deliberated in the Diet.

notes:
USAGE:
A legal term used in academic, legal, and news contexts. Japan's {民法|みんぽう} was originally modeled on European civil law systems and has been revised multiple times, most recently regarding the age of majority and marriage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {民法|みんぽう}{改正|かいせい}: civil code revision
- {民法|みんぽう}の{規定|きてい}: provisions of the civil code
- {民法|みんぽう}{上|じょう}の: under civil law
- {民法|みんぽう}{学者|がくしゃ}: civil law scholar
